title: Rapid profiling field report: multiplexed short+long runs
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick field report from pair-run (me + Leo) to stress multiplexed traffic with mixed short and long requests. Trying to capture realistic app mix: many short assistants + occasional long summarizations. Goal: find knee of p95/p99 as concurrency increases and whether KV-cache + prefix coalescing helps p99 for short requests.

Hypothesis:
- Short requests (<=128 tokens) dominate tail when they queue behind long requests (>=1024 tokens) unless we preempt or isolate.
- Enabling prefix coalescing + active KV cache will reduce p99 for short requests by ~35–60% at moderate QPS.

Environment / infra:
- Model: open-variant-7b-fp16 (production-ish config), seq cap 2048, kv cache enabled.
- Hardware: mixed A10G pool + a few A100s on dedicated test cluster (4x A10G, 2x A100).
- Runtime: serving-runtime v0.32.1 (PR 1294 branch for coalescing).
- Traffic generator: locust-derived harness (custom), 48 workers, steady-state arrival patterns (poisson + small bursts).
- Observability: telemetry via Console dev dashboard, GPU exporter, and local run logs.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Mixes: short-only (100% <=128), mixed-90/10 (90% short, 10% long >=1024), long-only.
- Concurrency sweep: target QPS 50 -> 100 -> 200 -> 400 -> 800 (step up 10min each).
- Batching: runtime auto-batching on (default), batch cap 64.
- KV cache: off / on.
- Coalescing (PR): disabled / enabled.

Key run notes (timestamps local):
- 2026-02-10 09:10: cold cluster start; warmed with 120 short warmup requests (50 tokens each).
- 09:20: started short-only sweep. Observed GPU utilization 28–45% at QPS 50–200.
- 09:50: enabled mixed-90/10 at QPS 200 -> small tail increase visible.
- 10:10: toggled coalescing on; immediate p95 improvement for short path.

Representative numbers (mixed-90/10, A10G pool, batch cap 64):
- QPS 200, KV off, coalescing off:
  - short requests: p50 18ms, p95 220ms, p99 960ms
  - long requests: p50 980ms, p95 1.6s, p99 2.4s
- QPS 200, KV on, coalescing on:
  - short requests: p50 16ms, p95 120ms, p99 420ms
  - long requests: p50 960ms, p95 1.5s, p99 2.2s
- QPS 400, KV on, coalescing on:
  - short requests: p50 22ms, p95 220ms, p99 950ms (note: near knee)
  - long requests: p50 1.2s, p95 1.9s, p99 3.1s

Observed patterns and interpretation:
- Benefit of KV cache + coalescing concentrated on short path; p95 halved at 200 QPS. Suggests caching + prefix sharing avoided repeated attention compute on short prompts.
- At higher QPS (>=400) we hit multiplexing saturation: long requests get large KV/compute windows and starve small ones unless preemptive scheduling applied.
- Batch coalescing helps throughput but increases variability for mixed workloads without request-priority.
- GPU util increased from 45% -> 78% between 200 -> 400 QPS, but p99 for short requests spiked, implying queueing latency rather than compute.

Quick ASCII latency sketch (short requests, mixed-90/10):
Time -> |---QPS200---|---QPS400---|
p95(ms)  |   120       |   220      |
p99(ms)  |   420       |   950      |

Failure modes observed:
- Occasional long-run stragglers stuck in queue for 1.5–2x expected due to batch buildup (seen at 10:05-10:08).
- One incident of RPC timeouts to A10G node at 10:32 (investigating infra flakiness). Logged: PERF-842.

Actionable takeaways / short-term next steps:
1) Default release: enable KV cache and coalescing for HTTP short-path routes (can gate via feature flag). Reason: consistent p95 improvements without major long-run regression at moderate QPS.
2) Add request-priority lane for <=128 token requests (soft-preempt) — prototype scheduling knobs in runtime.
3) Tune batch cap downward when mixed ratio >70% short to avoid long-request-induced queuing. Experiment: batch cap 32 vs 64 at QPS 400.
4) Re-run on A100s only to isolate node-type impact (A100 latency better at high concurrency?).
5) Investigate RPC timeout and infra flakiness; correlate with node metrics and kube events.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How much of the improved short-path p95 is attributable solely to coalescing vs KV cache? Need A/B runs where we toggle one at a time for better attribution.
- Is soft-preempt scheduling sufficient or do we need strict lane isolation for enterprise workloads with hard SLOs?
- How do these findings generalize to quantized 4-bit models? Might change compute balance and queuing dynamics.

Notes to self:
- Capture per-batch composition (num short vs long) in telemetry for next run — add a metric in PR 1294.
- Add trace ids to a sample of 1% requests to reconstruct queue lifetime in distributed traces.
- Share a short summary with product-hosted-api and solutions-eng for input on default SLO decisions.

Quick links / refs:
- PR with coalescing prototypes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1294
- Jira: PERF-842 (timeout flake), PERF-859 (priority lanes proposal)

Bottom line (one-liner): KV cache + coalescing materially reduces short-request tails at moderate QPS; at high QPS, mixed long requests create queueing that requires scheduling/batching policy changes.

-- Amelia
